entities.title: Simara Chowk, Bara

properties.description: Junction in Bara district named in Kathmandu Post reporting on the 19 November 2025 clash between Gen Z activists and police. No coordinates were retrieved for it.
properties.coordinate_basis: No coordinates recorded; none retrieved from Wikipedia, Wikidata or OpenStreetMap in this pass.

entities.title: Bibeksheel Sajha Party

properties.description: Party headed by Samiksha Baskota. It announced a merger with the Rastriya Swatantra Party on 30 November 2025.

entities.title: High-level study committee on cases against Gen Z protesters

properties.description: Committee headed by former High Court judge Baburam Regmi, with former Deputy Attorney General Chet Nath Ghimire and retired DIG Poshraj Pokharel. It submitted its report to Home Minister Sudan Gurung on 1 October 2026.

entities.title: Committee to study security agencies' role on 8-9 September

properties.description: Committee formed by the cabinet on 15 April 2026 under former High Court judge Prem Raj Karki, with former APF AIG Subodh Adhikari and former police AIG Tek Prasad Rai, to study the inquiry findings and security mechanisms.

entities.title: GenZ Martyrs' Family Welfare Society

properties.description: Society that organised a programme in New Baneshwor on 8 September 2026, attended by the Home Minister, other ministers and families of the dead.

entities.title: National Council for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management

properties.description: Council chaired by Prime Minister Balendra Shah. In early October 2026 it recommended a Rs559.17 billion budget for 504 reconstruction plans after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods.

entities.title: Bigyan Raj Sharma

properties.profile: Former additional inspector general of police, member of the Karki inquiry commission.

evidence.note: Spelled Bigyan Raj, Bigyanraj and Bigyan Ran in different outlets.

entities.title: Bishweshwor Prasad Bhandari

properties.profile: Legal expert, member of the Karki inquiry commission.

evidence.note: Spelled Bishweshwar / Bishweshwor in different outlets.

entities.title: Ram Bahadur Thapa

properties.profile: CPN-UML vice-chair. In September 2026 he prepared a 39-page report arguing that Oli need not step down after the election defeat.

entities.title: Shankar Pokharel

properties.profile: CPN-UML general secretary. His 65-page report recommended that Oli take responsibility and step down (as described by Onlinekhabar). At the Nepali Congress convention in October 2026 he asked whether Nepal was moving towards authoritarianism.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post spells the surname Pokhrel.

entities.title: Yogesh Bhattarai

properties.profile: CPN-UML leader who told a secretariat meeting in May 2026 that the party could not move forward under Oli and that Oli should resign (reported indirectly).

entities.title: Ishwar Pokhrel

properties.profile: Oli's closest competitor in the December 2025 UML chair vote, with 564 votes against Oli's 1,663.

entities.title: Prem Raj Karki

properties.profile: Former High Court judge who heads the committee formed on 15 April 2026 to study the security agencies' role on 8-9 September.

entities.title: Baburam Regmi

properties.profile: Former High Court judge who headed the committee that reported on 1 October 2026 on criminal cases against Gen Z protesters.

entities.title: Ananda Shrestha

properties.profile: Judge of the Kathmandu District Court who issued the five-day remand order for Oli and Lekhak on 29 March 2026.

entities.title: Anup Kumar Upadhyay

properties.profile: Chief of the Ujyaalo Nepal Party, which announced unity with the RSP on 29 December 2025 and split from it on 10 January 2026.

entities.title: Samiksha Baskota

properties.profile: Head of the Bibeksheel Sajha Party, which announced its merger with the RSP on 30 November 2025.

entities.title: More than 6,800 escaped prisoners still at large

properties.summary: On 25 September 2025 officials said more than 6,800 people who escaped prisons and custody during the unrest remained at large; the director of the Department of Prison Management is quoted on the number rearrested. The numbers inside the one retrieved article are not consistent with each other (about 6,900 rearrested against about 7,300 recaptured).

evidence.note: One article; its recapture figures differ internally.

entities.title: Gen Z activists and police clash at Simara Chowk, Bara

properties.summary: Six Gen Z youths were injured in a clash after Gen Z activists protested at Simara Chowk in Bara. Police arrested three people, including two ward chairs elected from UML; three others remained at large. Gen Z leaders accused police of security lapses. A six-point verbal deal followed at the Armed Police Force Technical School in Pathahiya.

evidence.note: Date inferred: the article of Friday 21 November 2025 refers to 'Wednesday's clash'.

entities.title: Gen Z groups demand interim PM Karki's resignation

properties.summary: Onlinekhabar reports protesters chanting for Prime Minister Sushila Karki to resign outside Baluwatar, a riot-police charge on organisers, and a petition by 23 Gen Z groups to the President asking for her removal for sidelining the movement's core demands. It also reports an allegation of nepotism against her chief private secretary.

evidence.note: The article is dated 26 November 2025; the protest date itself is not given in the retrieved text, so precision is month.

entities.title: Ten left parties merge into the Nepali Communist Party

properties.summary: Ten left parties, including the CPN (Maoist Centre), merged into the Nepali Communist Party with Pushpa Kamal Dahal as coordinator and Madhav Kumar Nepal as co-coordinator. The Tribune ties the merger to the September uprising and the announced March elections. CPN-UML stayed out.

evidence.note: The UML exclusion is from the Wire/Tribune summary of the merger; the Kathmandu Post piece of 22 September 2025 only supports Maoist Centre's restructuring.

entities.title: RSP and Bibeksheel Sajha announce merger

properties.summary: The Rastriya Swatantra Party, led by Rabi Lamichhane, and the Bibeksheel Sajha Party, headed by Samiksha Baskota, announced their merger on 30 November 2025. The unified party keeps the RSP name and the bell symbol.

entities.title: Oli re-elected CPN-UML chair at 11th general convention

properties.summary: KP Sharma Oli was re-elected CPN-UML chairman at the party's 11th general convention with 1,663 votes against Ishwar Pokhrel's 564. Polling began on Wednesday 17 December and ended early on Thursday 18 December.

entities.title: Election Commission publishes final voters' roll

properties.summary: The Election Commission published the final voters' roll with 18,903,689 eligible voters, 915,119 more than in 2022, and designated 10,967 polling stations for the 5 March 2026 election.

entities.title: Ujyaalo Nepal Party splits from RSP

properties.summary: The Ujyaalo Nepal Party, widely considered Kulman Ghising's creation, formally split from the RSP on Saturday 10 January 2026, 12 days after the two parties announced unity under a seven-point agreement on 29 December 2025. The Kathmandu Post gives disagreement over distribution of portfolios as the sole reason.

entities.title: Nepali Congress special convention elects Gagan Thapa president

properties.summary: A special general convention elected Gagan Thapa Nepali Congress president as the only candidate on 14 January 2026. The same day the Deuba-aligned committee suspended Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma for five years. The Election Commission recognised the Thapa-led party on 16 January; the Deuba camp said it would contest this.

entities.title: House of Representatives election

properties.summary: Election to the 275-member House of Representatives, the first since the September 2025 uprising, held on the date set on 12 September 2025. Turnout was about 60 per cent. The RSP won 125 of 165 direct seats and 57 proportional seats, 182 in total; Nepali Congress 38; CPN-UML 25. Balendra Shah beat Oli in Jhapa-5 by 49,614 votes. Interim counts and analyst estimates ran ahead of the final total (an estimate of 185-190 seats on 9 March; 119 direct seats at an interim count).

evidence.note: Final totals from RTHK and Wikipedia; interim and forecast numbers differ and are described in the summary.

entities.title: Karki commission submits report on 8-9 September events

properties.summary: The three-member commission chaired by Gauri Bahadur Karki handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki on Sunday 8 March 2026, after questioning about 200 people. Outlets give different lengths (1,000 pages; 8,000-10,000 pages). The report recommended criminal investigation of Oli, Lekhak and Khapung under Sections 181 and 182, and departmental action against police, Armed Police and Army officers. After outlets published its content, Karki decided on about 25 March to release it formally.

evidence.note: Report length is disputed; see the two report-length claims.

entities.title: Balendra Shah sworn in as prime minister

properties.summary: President Ram Chandra Paudel swore in Balendra Shah (35, RSP) as prime minister on Friday 27 March 2026. Fourteen ministers took the oath at the ceremony, with Sudan Gurung as home minister. Sushila Karki had left office the same week.

evidence.note: Cabinet size is reported as 15 including the prime minister (Hitavada: 14 others) while another search result said 16; ShareSansar's lineup piece mentions 11 portfolios.

entities.title: Former PM Oli and former Home Minister Lekhak arrested

properties.summary: Nepal Police arrested Oli and Lekhak early on Saturday 28 March 2026 from their homes in Bhaktapur, after the new cabinet decided to implement the commission report, in a case of negligence leading to deaths on 8 September 2025. Outlets differ on whether the warrants were issued by a court or were urgent warrants awaiting validation, and on the Penal Code sections.

evidence.note: Arrest itself is consistent across outlets. Warrant type and Penal Code sections are disputed (see claims).

entities.title: UML secretariat meeting debates Oli's leadership

properties.summary: At a UML secretariat meeting reported on 24 May 2026, Yogesh Bhattarai said the party could not move forward under Oli and that he should resign (reported indirectly by Spotlight Nepal).

evidence.note: Date is the article date; the meeting date is not given.

entities.title: Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods

properties.summary: Floods on the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers in August 2026. By 5 October 2026 the government had suspended search and rescue except in emergencies and was moving to reconstruction. Not linked in the sources to the September 2025 protests; recorded because it is the main current crisis in the dataset's final weeks.

evidence.note: Month taken from Africanews's reference to August floods (not quoted); the Kathmandu Post article does not give a date.

entities.title: First anniversary: Gen Z Martyrs' Day

properties.summary: Nepal observed 8 September 2026 as Gen Z Martyrs' Day, a public holiday. A programme by the GenZ Martyrs' Family Welfare Society in New Baneshwor was attended by the Home Minister, ministers and families. Hamro Patro says 76 people died and the government has declared 45 martyrs; embassies including Australia, Norway, the UK, the US and Japan posted messages. An injured protester told Africanews the injured still needed state support.

evidence.note: Death toll given as 76 by Hamro Patro and 77 by IANS.

entities.title: Parties issue contrasting statements on the anniversary

properties.summary: On 8-9 September 2026 the RSP and Lamichhane stressed state repression and the spontaneity of the movement; Oli described the 9 September destruction as the result of a planned attempt; Pushpa Kamal Dahal said the two days should not be viewed the same way; Gagan Thapa sent a video tribute. IANS summarises that the RSP played down property destruction while opposition parties stressed it.

entities.title: UML vice-chair and general secretary submit opposing reports on Oli

properties.summary: Vice-chair Ram Bahadur Thapa's 39-page report defended Oli and said losing an election does not require the chair to resign. General Secretary Shankar Pokharel's 65-page report recommended Oli step down.

evidence.note: One article, dated 11 September 2026; the Pokharel report is described only by the article.

entities.title: Nepali Congress 15th general convention

properties.summary: Leaders of the Congress, RSP, Nepali Communist Party and UML spoke at the Congress general convention at Khula Manch (Tundikhel), pledging cooperation on democracy and the constitution. Gagan Thapa criticised the prime minister's absence from Parliament; Dahal and UML's Pokharel raised fears of authoritarianism. Thapa's interview of the same date places the start on 6 October and refers to a parallel convention by Sher Bahadur Deuba.

evidence.note: The Kathmandu Post's convention report is dated 5 October and quotes speeches, while its interview of 5 October says the convention begins on 6 October.

entities.title: Government forms inquiry commission under Gauri Bahadur Karki

properties.description: Three-member high-level commission formed on 21 September 2025 under Gauri Bahadur Karki with a three-month mandate to identify causes of the violence, vandalism, looting and arson and recommend action. Members: Bigyan Raj Sharma and Bishweshwor Prasad Bhandari. It reported on 8 March 2026, about five and a half months after formation; the retrieved sources do not say whether the deadline was extended.

evidence.note: The three-month mandate and the March report date differ; no retrieved source explains it.

entities.title: Dahal proposes dissolving all Maoist Centre committees

properties.description: Pushpa Kamal Dahal proposed dissolving all existing committees of the Maoist Centre and electing all office bearers directly at the general convention. The Kathmandu Post calls it the first party restructuring after the uprising.

entities.title: Passports of Oli and four officials frozen

properties.description: The government froze the passports of Oli, Ramesh Lekhak, former home secretary Gokarna Mani Duwadi, former National Investigation Department chief Hutaraj Thapa and former Kathmandu chief district officer Chhabi Rijal in connection with the suppression of the 8-9 September protests.

evidence.note: Which body issued the order is not stated in the retrieved text.

entities.title: Petitions at Supreme Court challenge Karki government and House dissolution

properties.description: The Supreme Court received 14 writ petitions on 15 October 2025; ten related to House dissolution and government formation and sought to reinstate Parliament and revoke Karki's appointment. No ruling was reported in the retrieved article.

entities.title: Cabinet declares 45 of the dead martyrs

properties.description: A cabinet meeting on Monday 3 November 2025 declared 45 people who died in the movement martyrs, based on a Home Ministry committee study with security agencies and district administration offices. The Kathmandu Post gives 76 deaths in total.

entities.title: Gen Z youth and Bara security committee reach six-point verbal deal

properties.description: At talks at the Armed Police Force Technical School in Pathahiya, officials agreed to address all six demands raised by Gen Z youth after the Simara clash. The date is the article date.

entities.title: Agreement to release those charged only for joining the protests

properties.description: The Kathmandu Post of 5 October 2026 says a 10 December 2025 agreement stipulated that people under investigation or charged purely for taking part in the 8-9 September protests would be released. The parties to the agreement are not named in the retrieved text.

evidence.note: Only one article, and it does not name the signatories.

entities.title: Kulman Ghising resigns as energy minister

properties.description: Energy Minister Kulman Ghising resigned on 7 January 2026, reportedly after Prime Minister Karki asked ministers considering contesting the 5 March election to resign. He said he had not yet taken RSP membership.

entities.title: Deuba-aligned committee suspends Gagan Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma

properties.description: The central working committee suspended general secretaries Gagan Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma and joint general secretary Farmullah Mansur for five years for calling the special general convention without the establishment faction's consent. The special convention hall annulled the action, according to a search-result summary of another outlet.

entities.title: Election Commission recognises Thapa-led Nepali Congress

properties.description: The Election Commission recognised the Gagan Thapa-led Nepali Congress as the legitimate party, citing the statute's special-convention provision, delegates' supreme authority and no recorded dissent over the convening. The Deuba camp said it would fight the ruling.

evidence.note: Single retrieved article; a search-result summary says the Supreme Court later recognised the Thapa faction, not retrieved here.

entities.title: Election code of conduct 2026 enforced

properties.description: The Election Commission enforced the Election Code of Conduct, 2026 from 19 January for the 5 March House of Representatives election.

entities.title: HRW, Amnesty and ICJ urge publication of reports on the crackdown

properties.description: The three organisations urged the interim government to publish all reports documenting violations against protesters and asked parties to commit to ending impunity. HRW says at least 76 people were killed.

entities.title: Prime Minister Karki decides to publish the commission report

properties.description: Himal Press reports the prime minister decided on Wednesday evening to publish the report, after media outlets had published it. The Kathmandu Post reported the leaked content on 26 March. The Wednesday is taken to be 25 March from the article date.

entities.title: Cabinet decides to implement the commission report

properties.description: After Balendra Shah's swearing-in, a cabinet meeting decided to implement the report of the High-Level Inquiry Commission, recommending criminal investigation and prosecution of Oli, Lekhak and Khapung. IANS says the meeting was held 'on the same day' as the arrests (28 March), which conflicts with other summaries placing it after the swearing-in on 27 March.

evidence.note: Date is 27 or 28 March; one retrieved source, with the 27 March reading from the sequence of events.

entities.title: Arrest of Oli and Lekhak on negligence charges

properties.description: Nepal Police arrested Oli and Lekhak at their homes in Bhaktapur. Home Minister Sudan Gurung said it was not revenge. Oli said it was retaliatory.

evidence.note: Warrant type and Penal Code sections differ between outlets.

entities.title: Kathmandu District Court grants five-day remand

properties.description: A single bench of judge Ananda Shrestha remanded Oli and Lekhak to five days in custody. Prosecutors had sought 10 days. Lekhak appeared in person; Oli, being treated at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, appeared virtually. Defence lawyers said there were no grounds for detention.

entities.title: Government announces 100-point governance roadmap

properties.description: The roadmap includes a rehabilitation package for Gen Z protest victims (employment, skill development, psychosocial counselling) and the immediate start of investigations and legal action based on the Karki commission report.

entities.title: Supreme Court declines to release Oli and Lekhak

properties.description: The Supreme Court declined on Monday 30 March to release the two after petitions alleging illegal detention, according to OCCRP.

entities.title: House elects Dol Prasad Aryal Speaker

properties.description: Dol Prasad Aryal of the RSP was declared elected unopposed as Speaker.

entities.title: Supreme Court orders investigation concluded or suspects freed

properties.description: On Monday 6 April the Supreme Court ruled that authorities must either formally conclude the investigation or free the suspects, citing health, equal treatment with others released in similar cases, and that the main investigative steps were done.

entities.title: Oli and Lekhak released on condition of availability

properties.description: Authorities released Oli and Lekhak on Thursday 9 April after about two weeks of detention, on the condition that they remain available to investigators. Kantipur notes this is release from custody, not from charges. The Kathmandu Post quotes Oli saying he was detained unlawfully for 13 days.

entities.title: Cabinet forms committee to study security agencies' role

properties.description: A cabinet meeting on Wednesday 15 April formed a committee under former High Court judge Prem Raj Karki, with former APF AIG Subodh Adhikari and former police AIG Tek Prasad Rai, to study the commission report and security mechanisms.

entities.title: Sudan Gurung resigns as home minister

properties.description: Gurung resigned over scrutiny of his financial dealings and alleged ties to a businessman under money-laundering investigation, to allow an impartial investigation. Prime Minister Shah took the Home portfolio in the interim.

entities.title: Government finalises list of 2,660 injured

properties.description: The government finalised the verified injured list at 2,660. Of 250 names recently recommended, 22 were approved. Recognised injured are eligible for quotas in education, employment and medical treatment.

entities.title: Probe committee clears Gurung

properties.description: A committee investigating Gurung's finances concluded the allegations could not be substantiated; the Kathmandu Post says it did not consider his landholdings unusual or suspicious, and IANS says it found no established link to the businessman. The report date is not given; the date here is the day of the reappointment reports.

entities.title: Gurung reappointed home minister; Pun appointed minister
